subject: pebble toad
title: This Toad Can't Outrun a Tarantula, So It Throws Itself Down a Mountain

scenes.text: This toad escapes by throwing itself off a mountain.
The pebble toad lives on top of two table mountains in Venezuela, more than 7,500 feet up.
It's about an inch long, a poor jumper, and no match for a tarantula.
So when one comes close, the toad tucks in its legs, tenses into a ball and lets go.
It bounces down the rock face like a pebble.
It's so light that the impacts are too weak to hurt it. It gets up and walks away.

description:
The pebble toad escapes predators by curling into a ball and tumbling down a mountain.
Oreophrynella nigra is known from just two tepuis in Venezuela, Kukenan and Yuruani, at 2,300 to 2,700 meters. Adults measure about 16 to 30 millimeters. When threatened it folds its limbs under its body, tucks in its head and tenses, and on a slope it simply rolls away; the BBC series Life filmed one escaping a tarantula this way in 2009. Because the toad is so small and light, the forces of each impact are too tiny to injure it.
What is the strangest escape trick you know? Comment below.
first_comment: The toad is also a weak swimmer, so the one bad place to land is a deep pool. What is the strangest escape trick you know?
